# QUESTIONs with `tags` `learning-theory`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Learning theory** — why learning generalizes and how it proceeds — compression and description length, Kolmogorov complexity and sufficient statistics, rate–distortion and PAC-style bounds, model selection; and training dynamics: solvable models of learning trajectories, stages, plateaus and phase transitions in training, and the implicit bias of optimisation. A work whose subject is how to train a model better is ML practice and goes to the anthology (ADR-036).

| [QUESTION-080](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-080.md) | When a trained network's parameters keep moving after its loss has converged, what about the network stays fixed, and is the last-layer geometry of neural collapse among the things that do? | The record holds two pictures of the end of training. In one, the last layer converges to a fixed geometry through the terminal phase ([THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), neural collapse). In the other, the parameters never stop: they sample a stationary distribution at constant speed ([THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)). The two may describe different regimes. The terminal phase of neural collapse is cross-entropy training past zero error, with no finite minimum, while the limiting dynamics assume a quadratic minimum. Nothing in the record relates them. Drawn by the assistant from the reading of Kunin et al., and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) | When the relative scale of a network's layers sets its learning regime under gradient flow, does that regime survive SGD, whose minibatch noise drives the relative scale toward balance, and on what timescale compared with learning? | Two readings meet here. Under gradient flow, the relative scale of adjacent layers is conserved and sets whether learning is rich or lazy ([THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md), Dominé et al.). Under SGD, that scale is not conserved: minibatch noise drives it toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances, at a rate set by η/S ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md), Ziyin et al.). If the drift is fast compared with learning, an unbalanced start chosen to be lazy would drift toward balance and richness. If it is slow, the regime set at initialization stands. Neither paper addresses the other. Drawn by the assistant from reading both, and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) v4 | When the record meets a random linear map that keeps what a later stage needs, in random features for kernels, the compressed-sensing bound on superposition, and the expand-and-threshold codes of sparse distributed memory and the fly, is it one concentration-of-measure fact applied to different families, and does each threshold count the same thing? | Filed when a survey of the record found random projections in three places and the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma in none. The three uses carry three thresholds: ε⁻² log n for distances, k log(n/k) for sparse recovery, and 2N = n for random-features regression. The question is whether these are one union bound over different families or different phenomena that share a tool. Six anchor works are now read. They show the distance and sparse-recovery thresholds share a sufficiency proof, but not a necessity proof, and give nothing that reaches the other two uses. For SDM and the fly, the record's SDM recall account and its LSH account offer candidate thresholds of a different shape. | Open |
| [QUESTION-122](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-122.md) | Can a deep network during training have meaningful affect-like states, such as frustration of its demands, and to which unit, the network, the network–optimizer pair or the training process, would they belong? | The owner's, U30 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "the possibility of meaningful affective states attributable to a deep neural network specifically during training". | [QUESTION-133](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-133.md) | Can a population of operators whose demands are jointly infeasible under one functional organization develop a differentiated or compositional repertoire that makes them jointly feasible, without suppressing, weakening or deleting any of those demands? | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18, which called it the most conceptually interesting new connection. [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) defines structural frustration as joint infeasibility and relief as enlargement of the compatibility complex under fixed demands. [CASE-119](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-119.md) shows relief by enlarging the attainable set, with every pair compatible and the triple not, until a composite policy appears. The question is whether learning, specialization or recomposition can bring this about endogenously. An answer is a model that keeps the acceptance sets fixed while learning changes what is attainable and strictly enlarges the complex. Apparent relief that comes only from removing a demand or redefining success does not count. | Open |
| [QUESTION-134](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-134.md) | When influence decides access to learning opportunities, does the resulting feedback make a marginalized specialist lose its competence, so that it cannot recover influence even when its former niche becomes relevant again? | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18. [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md)'s note of 2026-10-18 records niche exclusion by authority deprivation: low exposure, poor competence estimates, low endorsement, lower exposure. This asks whether the loop goes further and destroys the competence, not just the measurement of it. When training opportunities follow influence, a specialist denied opportunities may become genuinely unable to do its job. An answer separates loss of influence, loss of competence and loss of access to evaluation. That gives an operational test for one mechanism of domination without defining domination as holding less authority. | Open |
